sentences.text: Dated this the 7th day of August, 2025 The writ petition is preferred, being aggrieved by the issuance of Ext.P18, whereby the earlier order passed by the Special Tahsildar (LA) for the Cochin Metro Rail Project was unsettled.

2. In fact, the property belonging to the petitioners, who are husband and wife, has been notified for the purpose of acquisition for the Cochin Metro Rail Project under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Since the award was not made prior to 01.01.2014, the entire acquisition proceedings were considered under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the '2013 Act').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Since the rules pertaining to the 2013 Act had not been framed, the property was taken under the Negotiated Purchase Scheme.

Altogether, 15.227 Ares were taken from the petitioners, however, for 0.223 ..4..
2025:KER:60595 Ares of the property, the petitioners could not produce any title deeds.

sentences.text: It is contended by the petitioners that the entire property belonging to the husband and wife is situated within the compound wall, and that the property described in the husband's title deed is less than what is actually available, whereas a certain extent, i.e., 0.223 Ares, is in excess of the property described in the wife's title deed.
However, by Ext.P9 order, taking into consideration the 0.223 Ares of property, they paid 80% of the amount; what remains is 20% of the amount.

In this regard, a legal opinion has already been produced as Ext.P10, in which the District Government Pleader opined that if one scale of measurement is chosen, the same has to be followed throughout,
and that it is not correct to accept the survey demarcation for disbursing compensation to Sri E.P.
George while relying on the title deed for computing compensation to Smt. Ann George.
4.
Hence, the application of the parties advised to be considered, and compensation for 0.223 Ares of property ..

5..
2025:KER:60595 also advised to disbursed to them.

Subsequently, on the basis of the objection raised by the Metro Rail Corporation, as there was no title deed for this extent of 0.223 Ares, the Special Tahsildar (LA) revisited the order passed by the same authority without any interference from any court of law.

According to the petitioners, it is against the principles of law, as the Special Tahsildar (LA), being functus officio, cannot revisit the order at a later point in time without setting aside the earlier order by any competent authority.
The reason pointed out for revisiting the order is that, for the extent of 0.223 Ares, the petitioners could not produce any title deeds.

These are the circumstances in which the writ petition has been filed, challenging Ext.P18.
5.

In response to the contentions, the learned counsel for the 4th respondent has filed a counter affidavit and submitted that, if the 1st petitioner proves her title over the disputed 0.223 Ares of the property by a valid document, the 4 th respondent has no objection in paying the sale consideration for that extent as well.

They are already concerned with obtaining a perfect title to ..6..
2025:KER:60595 the property purchased by paying a substantial sum of public money.
6. In reply to that the counsel for the petitioners brought to attention of this Court to a reported decision in State of Kerala v. Kuruvila [2005 (3) KLT 580].

entities.text: State of Kerala v. Kuruvila [2005 (3) KLT 580]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph No.8 of the said decision reads as follows:
"........8.
Now, we will consider the dispute regarding the area of the land acquired.
The Government had not, in respect of the property taken possession from the claimant, given notice to anyone else having interest in the property.
Necessarily, the claimant alone is having interest in the entire area taken from his possession.
It is an admitted case that the area taken in possession from the claimant had been compounded on all the four sides with well built walls.
It was his residential plot.
It is seen from Ext. C1 that the area so lying within the compound wall and acquired from the claimant was 22.464 cents.
There is no objection filed by the State to Ext. C1.
Necessarily, we have to accept such evidence on record as contained in Ext. C1 with regard to the area.
It is the only evidence available concerning the area taken from his possession.

The contention of the Government Pleader that the claimant did have Ann George vs The Special Tahsildar (La) on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97901224/
3 title over 18 cents alone is no answer when the area taken possession from the claimant extends to 22.454 cents and when the State had not given notice regarding the interest in the property to anyone else.

entities.text: Ann George vs The Special Tahsildar (La)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, we have to conclude that the land taken possession from the claimant from his occupation extends to 22 cents equivalent to 8.94 Ares.

Necessarily, the balance area in excess of that mentioned in the title deed ..7..
2025:KER:60595 executed in the year 1964 taken from his possession within his compound walls had been in his possession for about more than 35 years.

Therefore,
he had, on that strength of possession as well, entitlement for the compensation in respect of that area."

Going by the said decision, it appears that even if there is no title to certain extent of the property that is acquired, if it is within the compound wall and possession has been taken, it must be compensated.
However, in this case, it is not under any land acquisition proceedings but property was taken into possession under the Negotiated Purchase Scheme.
That is the reason why the 4th respondent is looking for a perfect title to the property.

7. In my considered opinion, since possession has been taken and the property is well within the boundary wall of the petitioners, and as there is no adverse claim against the said extent of 0.223 Ares, the subsequent decision by the same officer, made solely on the ground of absence of a title deed, cannot be sustained without the earlier order being set aside by another competent officer in respect of the same land.
8. Under such circumstances, Ext.P18 is set aside, and it is hereby directed that the 3rd respondent shall consider the ..8..
2025 :KER:60595 matter by treating Ext.P9 as an award
and shall deposit the amount due before the competent authority under Act 30 of the 2013 Act.
Any steps to recover the amount, if any, already paid shall not be effected in view of the setting aside of Ext.P18.
The District Collector shall deposit the amount due before the competent authority under the 2013 Act and shall disburse the amount in accordance with law.

The writ petition is disposed of as above.
Sd/-
P.M.MANOJ JUDGE sss ..9..
